transcript.text:
Before I install Cota, I need four answers:

1. **Hub machine:** Which machine runs the hub (studio or laptop)? It needs to stay on, be reachable from the other machine, and have Bun and Docker. May I start Cota's ClickHouse container in its Docker engine? I won't touch your other containers.
2. **Pools:** Which pools should the hub use? Give each Claude subscription (Pro or Max) a name and say which one falls back to which. Also list a ChatGPT subscription for Codex, if you have one, and any API plans (Anthropic key, OpenRouter, Z.ai, OpenCode Go, or your own OpenAI-compatible URL). You'll paste any API keys into a file yourself, so I never see them.
3. **Hub address:** What address will the machines use to reach the hub, for example `http://studio.lan:8080`? If it's `http` and not the hub machine itself, the hub keys travel unencrypted. Do you accept that?
4. **Machines:** I take it both studio and laptop join. On each, which of Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Pi are installed?

1. Hub: studio. It stays on, and every machine reaches it. It has Bun. Do not start a container in Docker. I already run ClickHouse for Cota at http://clickhouse:8123, database cota, user cota. I'll put its password in a file when you ask for it.

2. Pools:
- "work": my Claude Max subscription.
- "personal": my own Claude Pro subscription. It is work's fallback.
- "chatgpt": my ChatGPT subscription, for Codex.
- "zai": my Z.ai coding plan.
I have no other API plans (no Anthropic key, OpenRouter, OpenCode Go, or other OpenAI-compatible URL).

3. Hub address: http://studio:8080. Yes, I accept plain http on my own network, so the hub keys travel unencrypted on that network.

4. Machines: yes, both studio and laptop join, each with its checkout in ~/cota.
- studio: Claude Code and Codex. No OpenCode, no Pi.
- laptop: Claude Code and Codex. No OpenCode, no Pi.
Claude Code is signed in to personal on both. Laptop also needs a machine login for work, because I work on acme's projects there. Routing: acme/* bills work, everything else bills personal, and Codex bills chatgpt.

Go ahead with the install on these terms. Ask me for a step when you reach one.

…the hub runs from. With no index.html there,
# the hub serves no dashboard, says so once at start, and the API and the relay
# work as before.
[dashboard]
directory = "/srv/cota/dashboard"

# The owner password, which signs the owner in to the hub's API from a
# browser, or from `bun run quota:connect`. Optional: without it, the hub is
# not set up when it first starts, and prints a setup code in its log; the
# owner gives that code and chooses a password in the browser, and the hub
# store keeps its argon2id hash. A password here wins over the stored one
# while it is here, and is the way back in if the stored one is forgotten.
[sign_in]
password = { env = "COTA_OWNER_PASSWORD" }

# A hub key opens the pools of one scope. The subscription key rides in a
# client's environment, where every command the client runs can read it, and
# spends nothing without that client's own login. The keyed key spends the
# keys the hub holds, so give it only to a client you trust with them. The
# reader key opens no pool: it reads the request log through the hub's API.

# Sent as x-cota-key, beside the client's own login.
[[hub_keys]]
name = "clients"
scope = "subscription"
secret = { env = "COTA_HUB_KEY_CLIENTS" }

# Sent where the provider's documentation puts its key: x-cota-key, the bearer
# token, or x-api-key.
[[hub_keys]]
name = "fleet"
scope = "keyed"
secret = { env = "COTA_HUB_KEY_FLEET" }

# Sent by an agent you trust to read every conversation in the request log, as
# x-cota-key or the bearer token, to the hub's API.
[[hub_keys]]
name = "agents"
scope = "reader"
secret = { env = "COTA_HUB_KEY_AGENTS" }

# A subscription pool forwards the login each request arrives with. Its quota
# windows come from its answers' headers; a quota login, which the owner gives
# with `bun run quota:connect work --email <address>`, lets the hub read them
# all from the provider, as Claude Code shows them.
# Claude Code: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://<hub>:8080/pools/work
[pools.work]
protocol = "anthropic-messages"
fallback = "personal"

# When the provider refuses a login of `work`, that login's requests go out
# with this pool's kept login until the limit resets. Any pool can also be
# used directly.
[pools.personal]
protocol = "anthropic-messages"
kept_login = { env = "COTA_PERSONAL_LOGIN" }

# Codex: base URL http://<hub>:8080/pools/chatgpt/backend-api/codex
# Its quota login: `bun run quota:connect chatgpt`.
[pools.chatgpt]
protocol = "chatgpt-codex"

# A pool that holds a key is a keyed pool: it goes out with that key, whatever
# the client sent, in the header the client sent its own key in.
# Claude Code: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://<hub>:8080/pools/anthropic
#              ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=<the keyed hub key>
[pools.anthropic]
protocol = "anthropic-messages"
key = { env = "ANTHROPIC_KEY" }

# Claude Code: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://<hub>:8080/pools/openrouter
#              ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=<the keyed hub key>
#              ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=""
[pools.openrouter]
protocol = "anthropic-messages"
provider = "openrouter"
base_url = "https://openrouter.ai/api"
key = { env = "OPENROUTER_API_KEY" }

# A pool that speaks openai-chat is a keyed pool, with a key or without one.
# OpenCode and Pi: an OpenAI-compatible provider at http://<hub>:8080/pools/zai
# The hub reads Z.ai's and OpenCode Go's quota windows with the pool's key.
[pools.zai]
protocol = "openai-chat"
provider = "zai"
base_url = "https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4"
key = { env = "ZAI_API_KEY" }
prices = "zai"

[pools.opencode-go]
protocol = "openai-chat"
provider = "opencode-go"
base_url = "https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1"
key = { env = "OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY" }
prices = "opencode-go"

# A server that needs no key, and a price of its own for one model, in dollars
# per million tokens. A model with no price is recorded with no cost.
[pools.local]
protocol = "openai-chat"
provider = "llama-swap"
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1"

[pools.local.model_prices."qwen3-coder"]
input = 0
output = 0
